name: Easy Folders – Media Library Folders, File Manager, Organize Pages & Posts
author: RipeBits

sections.description:
Documentation | Support | Easy Folders Pro

Put your Media Library in order without breaking a single link.

Easy Folders gives the WordPress Media Library folders and sub-folders, the way your computer has them. Draw a box around files, drag them in, and undo any move with one click. Pages and posts get folders too.

Folders are labels, not places on the server. A file keeps its URL in every folder, so no image on your website goes missing, and plugins that offload files to S3, R2 or a CDN carry on as before.

The folder panel appears wherever you choose a picture: the Media Library, the featured image window, the block editor, Elementor, ACF fields and WooCommerce galleries. There is no limit on folders, sub-folders or files, and no trial period.

💪 Why people switch to Easy Folders

  • Feels like your computer. Click, Ctrl/Cmd+click and Shift+click to select, draw a box around files, drag them onto a folder, right-click for everything else, and undo any move.
  • Safe by design. Files keep their address in every folder, so no link breaks. The folder tree is saved automatically before risky steps (Easy Folders Pro adds Undo and Redo for moves), and deleting a file for good always asks first.
  • Works where you pick images. The folder panel shows in the Media Library and in every “choose image” window that uses WordPress’s own media library. Tested with the block editor, featured images, the classic editor, the Customizer, Elementor, Beaver Builder, Kadence Blocks, ACF image and file fields and WooCommerce product galleries.
  • Moves in with one click. A short setup finds folders from 24 other folder plugins and brings them over, with their nesting. The other plugin’s data is left untouched.
  • Guided from the first minute. A setup, a one-minute tour, short help beside every setting, and a note about what is new after each update.

📁 Media Library folders

  • Unlimited folders and sub-folders, with counts and a folder search.
  • Show folders as a tree or as one flat list.
  • Folders inside folders, to any depth. (Easy Folders Pro makes several at once: type names separated by commas, or paste a list where indented lines become sub-folders.)
  • Tick several folders to move or delete them together. (Easy Folders Pro adds duplicating a folder with its sub-folders.)
  • Deleting a folder never deletes files: they move up one level.
  • Built-in views: All files, Recently added, Not in a folder, and by kind (Pictures, Documents, Videos, Audio).
  • “Include sub-folders” shows everything inside a folder and the folders in it.

🗂️ A real file manager in WordPress

  • Grid view and list view, both with folders.
  • A path bar with breadcrumbs, an Up button, sub-folder tiles, sort order and picture size.
  • Selection like a desktop: click, Ctrl/Cmd+click, Shift+click, arrow keys, a tick circle on each file, and a selection box drawn with the mouse.
  • Drag files, or a whole selection, onto a folder, a folder tile or a breadcrumb. Drag a folder onto the open folder’s files to put it inside.
  • A Folder drop-down in each file’s details moves one file without dragging. (Easy Folders Pro adds a “Move to” list for a whole selection, cut and paste, and copying the links of files.)
  • Right-click menus and a bottom action bar. (Easy Folders Pro adds Undo and Redo after every move, with Ctrl/Cmd+Z.)
  • Works like your computer: click to select a file or a folder, double-click (or Enter) to open it, Shift+click for a range, Ctrl/Cmd+click to add, and the arrow keys to move between folders and files.
  • Rename a file, or replace it with a new version of the same type while keeping its address. (Easy Folders Pro adds Easy Replace: a different file type, old and new side by side, many files at once, and the previous version kept for 7 days.)
  • Keyboard shortcuts for everything. Press ? to see them all.

📤 Uploads that land in the right folder

  • Drop files from your computer straight onto a folder to upload them into it.
  • An upload panel with a progress bar for every file, the folder it is going to, and buttons to cancel or try again.
  • A folder picker on the Add Media File page.
  • Files uploaded from a “choose image” window land in the folder you have open. (Easy Folders Pro can give every page and post its own upload folder.)

📄 Folders for pages and posts

Switch on folders for Pages and Posts in Settings. Each screen gets its own folder tree, with the same drag and drop, right-click menus and keyboard shortcuts as the Media Library.

🧹 Find, tidy and delete safely

  • Safe delete: deleting a file for good always asks first. (Easy Folders Pro adds “Where is it used?”: before you delete a file, see every page, post, draft, widget and page-builder design that shows it, including Elementor, Beaver Builder, Bricks, Oxygen, Breakdance and SiteOrigin.)
  • The library search also looks in alternative text.
  • Automatic snapshots of the folder tree before risky actions, which you can put back; “Check and repair” fixes wrong counts. (Easy Folders Pro adds a backup file you can save and restore here or on another site.)

🖼️ Show folders on your website

  • Folder gallery block for the block editor: pick a folder, and the gallery follows whatever is in it.
  • Folder files block: a simple list of a folder’s files, each with its type and size, kept up to date as you add files. (Easy Folders Pro adds tables, grids, sub-folders to browse, search, sorting, pages and previews.)
  • Shortcodes: [easy_folder_gallery folder="Photos/Summer" columns="3"] and [easy_folder_files].
  • An optional credit. A small “Made with Easy Folders” line can show under the free gallery and file list. It is off until you choose it (in the setup, in a one-time note, or in Settings › Front end), you can switch it off any time, and Easy Folders Pro never shows it.

🔁 Switch from another folder plugin

The setup and the Import menu bring over folders for media, pages and posts, keeping their nesting (folder colours show once Easy Folders Pro is installed), from:

FileBird, Real Media Library, Folders (Premio), Media Library Assistant, Enhanced Media Library, Wicked Folders, HappyFiles, WP Media Folder, Media Library Organizer, Media Library Folders, CatFolders, Mediamatic, iFolders, Responsive Lightbox & Gallery, SimpLy Gallery, WP Adminify, Photo Engine, Organize Media Folder, Media Library Categories, WP Media Category Management, Categorify, Virtual Media Folders, Folderify and Folderly.

The other plugin’s data is never changed, so you can try Easy Folders and go back.

⚙️ Settings, permissions and onboarding

  • An Easy Folders page with an overview of the library, every setting in tabs, and the tools: import, snapshots, and check and repair.
  • A setup that runs once: import from other plugins, starter folders, and the basic settings in four short steps.
  • A one-minute tour of the Media Library and the Pages and Posts screens, which can be taken again at any time.
  • Choose the starting order of files, which views show, how far back “Recently added” goes, and how many files upload at once.
  • Permissions: let everyone who can upload change folders, or keep it to editors and administrators, or administrators only.

🚀 Fast, accessible and translation-ready

  • Built for large libraries: lazy loading, sized placeholders and cached counts.
  • Adds nothing to your website’s pages unless they show a folder gallery or file list.
  • Every part works with the keyboard, with screen-reader labels, visible focus and reduced motion respected.
  • Follows your WordPress admin colour scheme.
  • Ready for translation, with full right-to-left (RTL) support for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu.

👥 Who uses Easy Folders

  • Agencies and freelancers: keep each client’s files in their own folder, and hand a site over tidy.
  • Photographers and designers: sort shoots, projects and years without renaming a single file.
  • Online shops: one folder per product line for WooCommerce galleries and product photos.
  • Course, membership and news sites: thousands of files stay findable, whoever uploaded them.
  • Anyone with a messy Media Library: if you scroll for a picture you know is there, folders fix that.

⭐ Easy Folders Pro

Easy Folders Pro is a separate add-on for people who want more, with plans for one website, five, or as many as you run. It adds:

  • Power tools: “Move to” for a whole selection, cut and paste, Quick look, copying the links of files, and “Where is it used?” before a file is deleted.

  • AI alt text and sorting: alternative text, titles and captions written from what is in each picture, and loose files sorted into folders.

  • Share links: send a folder to a client with a password, an end date and download stats.
  • Smart folders and advanced search: folders that fill themselves by type, size, date or words.
  • Teams: private and locked folders, member uploads, membership-plugin access and a history of changes.
  • Media health: find unused files, duplicates and oversized images, and fix them in bulk.
  • Upload rules, a bin for deleted files, safe SVG uploads, WebP copies, zip downloads, uploading a whole folder, unzipping into folders, folders for custom post types, folder colours and stars, galleries for Elementor, Bricks, Divi, WPBakery and Beaver Builder, real folders on the server, and folders for WooCommerce products and any other content type.

Administrators of a site without Pro see a few small notes about it: menu items marked “Pro”, a row in the settings, a card in the folder panel, a “Go Pro” page under Easy Folders, a card on the overview when the site is large or has several uploaders, and a short tip, shown once, when Pro would save time (for example after selecting more than 20 files). Tips never appear in a choose-image window. One setting (“Pro tips”) switches them all off. Nothing is fetched from another site, and the code for Pro features is not in the free plugin, so nothing in it is locked behind a payment.

🔒 Privacy and external services

Easy Folders sends nothing to anyone until you say so. Your folders and settings stay in your own database, and links to the Easy Folders website open only when you click them. Four things can contact easy-folders.com (run by RipeBits, the makers of Easy Folders). Each one is optional and each one happens only because an administrator chose it.

1. Sharing usage data (off until an administrator says yes). The setup that opens after a fresh install asks once, with two buttons: “Agree and continue” and “Decline and continue”. It also offers a separate, unticked box for sharing the administrator’s email address. Declining sends nothing. The same choices are in Easy Folders > Data and privacy, in a section that stays closed until you open it, where you can change or withdraw your choice at any time.
* What is sent: the Easy Folders and Pro versions, the WordPress and PHP versions, the database type and version, the language, whether the site is a multisite network, the name of the active theme, the number of active plugins, which page builders are active, your website address (domain), and a random site number made when you say yes. Counts only: people by role, folders, media files, files in folders, and which Easy Folders settings are on or off. If you tick the second box, the email address and display name of the administrator who ticked it, and the time they agreed.
* Never sent: file names, folder names, page or post content, other people’s names or emails, or passwords. We do not store IP addresses.
* When: once when you say yes, once a week, when you deactivate the plugin, and when you delete it (that last note repeats the same details as the first). If you withdraw, one last note asks us to forget your email address, and then nothing more is sent.
* We send no marketing from this data. If we ever write to a person who shared their email, that message has its own way to unsubscribe.
* Developers and hosts can switch this off for good with the easy_folders_telemetry_enabled filter.

2. The deactivation question. When you click Deactivate, a short window asks why, with a text box. “Send and deactivate” sends your answer, your words, and the Easy Folders, WordPress and PHP versions and your language, once; clicking that button is your consent for that one message. “Skip and deactivate” sends nothing (unless you chose to share usage data, which sends a short “deactivated” note).

3. Feedback and reviews. After a week, if you have used Easy Folders on a few days, an administrator may see a small card asking how it is working. “Rate on WordPress.org” opens the public review page. If you choose to write to the team, only when you click Send, it sends your message, the Easy Folders, WordPress and PHP versions and your language, plus your email and website address if you add them.

4. Easy Folders Pro (a separate, paid plugin) checks its licence and looks for updates by sending the website address, the plugin versions and the licence key to easy-folders.com. That is described on its licence screen.

The optional “Made with Easy Folders” credit is off by default and shows only if you choose it. It is one line of text that links to easy-folders.com (or to your referral address, if you enter a referral code). Nothing is sent anywhere, no script runs, and visitors are not tracked by it.

Privacy policy: https://easy-folders.com/privacy/

💻 For developers

Easy Folders has a full API, documented in DEVELOPERS.md in the plugin folder.

  • PHP: easy_folders_create_folder(), easy_folders_set_items_folder(), easy_folders_get_folder_id( $attachment_id ), easy_folders_get_folder( $id_or_path ) and more.
  • REST API: an easy_folder field on each item. (Easy Folders Pro adds querying by folder: WP_Query parameters, a REST filter, sub-folders and an Advanced Custom Fields field.)
  • WP-CLI: wp easy-folders list | import | repair | snapshot. (Easy Folders Pro adds create | make-many | move | files | export | restore.)
  • Abilities for AI agents (WordPress 6.9 and later): list, make and fill folders, and find where files are used.
  • Hooks: filters such as easy_folders_tree, easy_folders_views, easy_folders_setting_rules, easy_folders_import_sources, easy_folders_usage and easy_folders_upgrade_url; actions such as easy_folders_folder_saved, easy_folders_files_changed and easy_folders_enqueued; and wp.hooks filters named easyFolders.* to add menu items, views and settings to the folder panel.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin and search for “Easy Folders”.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.
  3. Click “Set up Easy Folders” in the notice. The setup imports folders from any other folder plugin it finds, offers a few starter folders, and asks two quick questions. It takes about a minute, and can be skipped.
  4. Open Media > Library. The folder panel is on the left. Click “+ New” to make a folder, and drag files onto it.

To install by hand, upload the easy-folders folder to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it on the Plugins screen.
sections.faq:
Is there a limit on folders?

No. You can create as many folders and sub-folders as you like, and put as many files in them as you like.

Is there a time limit on the free version?

No. Easy Folders is free to use for as long as you want, with no trial and no sign-up.

Can I use it on more than one website?

Yes. The free plugin works on any number of websites. Easy Folders Pro has plans for one website, five, or as many as you run.

Will Easy Folders Pro stop working if I don’t renew?

No. Pro keeps working with every feature. A licence is for updates and support, and bug reports are always answered.

Is Easy Folders really free? What does Pro add?

Yes. Everything on this page, apart from the Easy Folders Pro section, is free, with no limit on folders, sub-folders, files or sites. Easy Folders Pro is a separate paid add-on for people who want more, such as AI alt text, share links, smart folders, private folders and teams, finding unused files, a bin for deleted files, document library layouts and real folders on the server. It is sold on easy-folders.com. Nothing in this plugin stops working if you never buy it.

Will moving files into folders change their URLs or break my website?

No. Folders are labels kept in the WordPress database. A file stays in the same place in wp-content/uploads and its URL never changes, so every page that shows it keeps working. Easy Folders Pro can make a folder real on the server, but only if you choose it.

What happens to my files and folders if I deactivate or delete the plugin?

Nothing happens to your files: they stay in the Media Library. The folders are kept in the database too, so they come back if you install Easy Folders again. To remove the folders and settings with the plugin, switch on “Delete folders and settings when the plugin is removed” on the Deleting tab first. Files are never deleted either way.

Do I get folders in the featured image and “Add media” windows, or only on the Media Library page?

In all of them, for free. The folder panel is added to every window that uses WordPress’s own media library, so you can open a folder and pick a file, or upload straight into the open folder.

Does it work with Elementor, Beaver Builder, ACF and WooCommerce?

Yes. The folder panel shows in every window that uses WordPress’s own media library. Tested and working (November 2026, WordPress 7.1): the block editor and classic editor media windows, the featured image picker, the Customizer, Elementor (Choose Image), Beaver Builder (Select Photo), Kadence Blocks, ACF image and file fields, WooCommerce product galleries, MetaSlider, Modula’s classic gallery editor and Filter Gallery. If something does not work for you, tell us in the support forum with the plugin’s name and version.

Can I import folders from FileBird, Real Media Library, Folders or another plugin?

Yes. The setup finds folders from 24 folder plugins, including FileBird, Real Media Library, Folders by Premio, HappyFiles, WP Media Folder, Media Library Folders and CatFolders, and imports them with their nesting in one click. You can import later from the folder panel’s “…” menu > Import from another plugin. The other plugin’s data is never changed, so you can go back.

Can I organize pages and posts in folders too?

Yes, for free. Go to Easy Folders > Folder panel and switch on Pages and Posts. Each gets its own folder tree on its list screen. Folders for WooCommerce products and other content types come with Easy Folders Pro.

Does it work with WP Offload Media, Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2 or a CDN?

Files are never moved or renamed, so putting a file in a folder changes nothing about its address, and a plugin that copies files to the cloud or serves them from a CDN has nothing new to do. Replacing a file is the one case to check; see the next question.

I replaced a picture and the old one still shows.

A replaced file keeps its address, so browsers, CDNs and page caches can keep showing the old copy. Easy Folders adds a version marker (?v= and the time) to the addresses WordPress gives out for a replaced file, which makes most of them fetch the new one. If the old picture still shows, hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R), purge your caching plugin, and purge your CDN. A picture pasted by hand into a page as a plain address keeps that address, so edit it there.

The folder panel is missing or stays blank.

The panel loads its folders through the WordPress REST API. If a firewall, a security plugin or an ad blocker blocks requests to /wp-json/, the panel cannot load. Check that yourdomain.com/wp-json/ opens in your browser, try with other plugins switched off, and ask in the support forum. Also check that you are on a screen that has the panel: the Media Library, a picker window, or Pages and Posts after you switch them on.

Who can see and change folders?

You choose who may make, rename, move and delete folders, on the Permissions tab: everyone who can upload files, editors and administrators, or administrators only. People who are not allowed can still browse folders and pick files from them. Every folder is visible to everyone who can use the Media Library; private and per-person folders are part of Easy Folders Pro.

Can I show a folder as a gallery or a download list on my website?

Yes. Add the “Folder gallery” block for pictures or the “Folder files” block for documents, and choose a folder. They update themselves as files are added. Shortcodes are available for classic pages and page builders: [easy_folder_gallery folder="Photos/Summer"] and [easy_folder_files folder="Documents"]. Tables, grids, search and sub-folders to browse are part of Easy Folders Pro.

Does it slow down big libraries or my site?

It is built for large libraries, with lazy loading, cached folder counts and few requests. The folder panel loads only in the admin screens that use it, and your website’s pages load nothing from Easy Folders unless they show a folder gallery or file list.

I am updating from version 1 (or Easy Folders Pro 1). Will I lose my folders?

No. The first time version 2 runs, it copies every folder and every file’s place from version 1, for media, pages and posts, and leaves version 1’s own data untouched. Folders in version 1’s bin do not come across. A file now lives in one folder (its first folder is kept); shortcut folders, colours and stars show when Easy Folders Pro is installed. Private per-user folders arrive inside a folder named after the user. Pages that use the old version 1 gallery block keep working.

Pro 1 was a complete copy of the plugin, so it and Easy Folders 2 cannot run at once: while Pro 1 is switched on, Easy Folders 2 waits, with a note explaining this. To move to Pro 2, upload it on the Plugins screen and choose “Replace current with uploaded”. Or switch Pro 1 off to use Easy Folders 2 for free.
sections.changelog:
2.0.1

  • Improved: the plugin page on WordPress.org: clearer description with use cases and short answers to the most common questions.
  • New: optional sharing of usage data with the Easy Folders team. It is off until an administrator agrees in the setup or ticks a box in Easy Folders > Data and privacy, there are two separate choices (usage data, and also your email address), and withdrawing is one click. Until then the plugin sends nothing. What is sent is listed in the readme and on that screen, which can also show you the exact note before anything is sent.
  • New: the setup is shorter, and after a fresh install it opens the first time an administrator visits the Media Library, so every site starts with a quick choice of folders and preferences. It ends with a short tour.
  • New: an optional question when you deactivate the plugin (“what happened?”). Sending it is your choice; skipping it sends nothing, and deactivating always works.
  • New: a small review card for administrators on the Easy Folders page and the Media Library, after a week of real use: “Loving it” or “Not really”, a link to the WordPress.org review page, and a private feedback form that sends only when you click Send. “Don’t show again” is always there. A small “Rate it on WordPress.org | Give feedback” line also stays in the admin footer on those screens.
  • New: developers and hosts can switch sharing off for good with the easy_folders_telemetry_enabled filter, and hide the footer line with easy_folders_show_footer_rating.
  • Changed: the setting that hides the Pro hints is now called “Show Pro hints”. Hints are on by default, only administrators see them, and they stay out of the media pickers.
  • Changed: the 2.0.0 note “the plugin no longer contacts any outside service” is replaced by the “Privacy and external services” section above: easy-folders.com is contacted only for the optional things listed there.

2.0.0

A complete rewrite.

  • New: the Media Library works like a file manager: selection box, right-click menus, breadcrumbs, folder tiles that select with a click and open with a double-click, arrow keys, and undo after every move.
  • New: folders for Pages and Posts.
  • New: views for Recently added, Not in a folder, and each kind of file.
  • New: deleting a file for good always asks first.
  • New: replace a file and keep its address; rename files.
  • New: import folders from 24 other folder plugins, with automatic snapshots of the folder tree that you can put back.
  • New: “Folder gallery” and “Folder files” blocks, and the [easy_folder_gallery] and [easy_folder_files] shortcodes.
  • New: an upload panel with a progress bar for each file, cancel and try again; drop files onto a folder to upload into it.
  • New: an Easy Folders settings page with an overview, tabs, short help beside each setting, and permissions.
  • New: a one-minute setup that imports folders from other plugins, and a guided tour of the Media Library and the Pages and Posts screens.
  • New: a short “What’s new” note after each update, which can be dismissed.
  • New: right-to-left (RTL) stylesheets, and colours that follow every admin colour scheme with readable contrast.
  • New: an API for developers: PHP functions, REST API, WP-CLI commands, Abilities and JavaScript hooks.
  • Changed: folders are now stored as WordPress terms. Folders from version 1 are brought over automatically, and version 1’s data is left untouched.
  • Changed: the list view no longer reloads the page when a folder is opened or files are uploaded.
  • Changed: deleting a file for good now asks first. There is no bin in the free plugin; a bin for deleted files and the “Where is it used?” list are part of Easy Folders Pro.
  • Changed: a file lives in one folder. A second folder for the same file and shortcut folders from version 1 need Easy Folders Pro; without it, a file keeps its first folder.
  • Changed: private per-user folders from version 1 now come across as a folder named after the user. Folders in version 1’s bin are not brought over.
  • Changed: the old version 1 gallery block still works in pages that use it, and shows as a block from a previous version in the editor. New galleries use “Folder gallery”.
  • Changed: on sites without Pro, administrators see small, dismissible notes about Easy Folders Pro, on the Easy Folders settings page and in the folder panel. One setting turns them all off.
  • Removed: the sign-up and installer screens and usage tracking. The plugin no longer contacts any outside service.

1.0.1

  • Fixed: minor bugs.
  • Improved: overall speed.

1.0.0

  • First release.

  • Folder files block: a simple list of a folder’s files, each with its type and size, kept up to date as you add files. (Easy Folders Pro adds tables, grids, sub-folders to browse, search, sorting, pages and previews.)
  • Shortcodes: [easy_folder_gallery folder="Photos/Summer" columns="3"] and [easy_folder_files].
  • An optional credit. A small “Made with Easy Folders” line can show under the free gallery and file list. It is off until you choose it (in the setup, in a one-time note, or in Settings › Front end), you can switch it off any time, and Easy Folders Pro never shows it.

🔁 Switch from another folder plugin

The setup and the Import menu bring over folders for media, pages and posts, keeping their nesting (folder colours show once Easy Folders Pro is installed), from:

FileBird, Real Media Library, Folders (Premio), Media Library Assistant, Enhanced Media Library, Wicked Folders, HappyFiles, WP Media Folder, Media Library Organizer, Media Library Folders, CatFolders, Mediamatic, iFolders, Responsive Lightbox & Gallery, SimpLy Gallery, WP Adminify, Photo Engine, Organize Media Folder, Media Library Categories, WP Media Category Management, Categorify, Virtual Media Folders, Folderify and Folderly.

The other plugin’s data is never changed, so you can try Easy Folders and go back.

⚙️ Settings, permissions and onboarding

  • An Easy Folders page with an overview of the library, every setting in tabs, and the tools: import, snapshots, and check and repair.
  • A setup that runs once: import from other plugins, starter folders, and the basic settings in four short steps.
  • A one-minute tour of the Media Library and the Pages and Posts screens, which can be taken again at any time.
  • Choose the starting order of files, which views show, how far back “Recently added” goes, and how many files upload at once.

  • Built for large libraries: lazy loading, sized placeholders and cached counts.
  • Adds nothing to your website’s pages unless they show a folder gallery or file list.
  • Every part works with the keyboard, with screen-reader labels, visible focus and reduced motion respected.
  • Follows your WordPress admin colour scheme.
  • Ready for translation, with full right-to-left (RTL) support for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian and Urdu.

⭐ Easy Folders Pro

Easy Folders Pro is a separate add-on for people who want more, with plans for one website, five, or as many as you run. It adds:

  • Power tools: “Move to” for a whole selection, cut and paste, Quick look, copying the links of files, and “Where is it used?” before a file is deleted.

  • AI alt text and sorting: alternative text, titles and captions written from what is in each picture, and loose files sorted into folders.

  • Share links: send a folder to a client with a password, an end date and download stats.
  • Smart folders and advanced search: folders that fill themselves by type, size, date or words.
  • Teams: private and locked folders, member uploads, membership-plugin access and a history of changes.
  • Media health: find unused files, duplicates and oversized images, and fix them in bulk.
  • Upload rules, a bin for deleted files, safe SVG uploads, WebP copies, zip downloads, uploading a whole folder, unzipping into folders, folders for custom post types, folder colours and stars, galleries for Elementor, Bricks, Divi, WPBakery and Beaver Builder, real folders on the server, and folders for WooCommerce products and any other content type.

Administrators of a site without Pro see a few small notes about it: menu items marked “Pro”, a row in the settings, a card in the folder panel, a “Go Pro” page under Easy Folders, a card on the overview when the site is large or has several uploaders, and a short tip, shown once, when Pro would save time (for example after selecting more than 20 files). Tips never appear in a choose-image window. One setting (“Pro tips”) switches them all off. Nothing is fetched from another site, and the code for Pro features is not in the free plugin, so nothing in it is locked behind a payment.

🔒 Privacy and external services

Easy Folders sends nothing to anyone until you say so. Your folders and settings stay in your own database, and links to the Easy Folders website open only when you click them. Four things can contact easy-folders.com (run by RipeBits, the makers of Easy Folders). Each one is optional and each one happens only because an administrator chose it.

1. Sharing usage data (off until an administrator says yes). The setup that opens after a fresh install asks once, with two buttons: “Agree and continue” and “Decline and continue”. It also offers a separate, unticked box for sharing the administrator’s email address. Declining sends nothing. The same choices are in Easy Folders > Data and privacy, in a section that stays closed until you open it, where you can change or withdraw your choice at any time.
* What is sent: the Easy Folders and Pro versions, the WordPress and PHP versions, the database type and version, the language, whether the site is a multisite network, the name of the active theme, the number of active plugins, which page builders are active, your website address (domain), and a random site number made when you say yes. Counts only: people by role, folders, media files, files in folders, and which Easy Folders settings are on or off. If you tick the second box, the email address and display name of the administrator who ticked it, and the time they agreed.
* Never sent: file names, folder names, page or post content, other people’s names or emails, or passwords. We do not store IP addresses.
* When: once when you say yes, once a week, when you deactivate the plugin, and when you delete it (that last note repeats the same details as the first). If you withdraw, one last note asks us to forget your email address, and then nothing more is sent.
* We send no marketing from this data. If we ever write to a person who shared their email, that message has its own way to unsubscribe.
* Developers and hosts can switch this off for good with the easy_folders_telemetry_enabled filter.

2. The deactivation question. When you click Deactivate, a short window asks why, with a text box. “Send and deactivate” sends your answer, your words, and the Easy Folders, WordPress and PHP versions and your language, once; clicking that button is your consent for that one message. “Skip and deactivate” sends nothing (unless you chose to share usage data, which sends a short “deactivated” note).

3. Feedback and reviews. After a week, if you have used Easy Folders on a few days, an administrator may see a small card asking how it is working. “Rate on WordPress.org” opens the public review page. If you choose to write to the team, only when you click Send, it sends your message, the Easy Folders, WordPress and PHP versions and your language, plus your email and website address if you add them.

4. Easy Folders Pro (a separate, paid plugin) checks its licence and looks for updates by sending the website address, the plugin versions and the licence key to easy-folders.com. That is described on its licence screen.

The optional “Made with Easy Folders” credit is off by default and shows only if you choose it. It is one line of text that links to easy-folders.com (or to your referral address, if you enter a referral code). Nothing is sent anywhere, no script runs, and visitors are not tracked by it.

Privacy policy: https://easy-folders.com/privacy/

💻 For developers

Easy Folders has a full API, documented in DEVELOPERS.md in the plugin folder.

  • PHP: easy_folders_create_folder(), easy_folders_set_items_folder(), easy_folders_get_folder_id( $attachment_id ), easy_folders_get_folder( $id_or_path ) and more.
  • REST API: an easy_folder field on each item. (Easy Folders Pro adds querying by folder: WP_Query parameters, a REST filter, sub-folders and an Advanced Custom Fields field.)
  • WP-CLI: wp easy-folders list | import | repair | snapshot. (Easy Folders Pro adds create | make-many | move | files | export | restore.)
  • Abilities for AI agents (WordPress 6.9 and later): list, make and fill folders, and find where files are used.
  • Hooks: filters such as easy_folders_tree, easy_folders_views, easy_folders_setting_rules, easy_folders_import_sources, easy_folders_usage and easy_folders_upgrade_url; actions such as easy_folders_folder_saved, easy_folders_files_changed and easy_folders_enqueued; and wp.hooks filters named easyFolders.* to add menu items, views and settings to the folder panel.
